meta.name: Lela conversation database
meta.note: Hand-written conversation data. It is not AI. Edit this file, then run: npm run db

levels.label: Beginner
levels.description: Short, simple sentences and slow speech.

levels.label: Advanced
levels.description: Detailed discussions, opinions, explanations and professional communication.

modes.label: Free Conversation
modes.description: Chat about anything: yourself, daily life, work and ideas.
modes.descriptionTamil: உங்களைப் பற்றி, அன்றாட வாழ்க்கை, வேலை, கருத்துகள் என எதைப் பற்றியும் பேசுங்கள்.

modes.label: Daily English Practice
modes.description: Everyday topics: routine, food, shopping, weather, hobbies.
modes.descriptionTamil: அன்றாட தலைப்புகள்: வழக்கம், உணவு, கடை, வானிலை, பொழுதுபோக்கு.

modes.label: Office English
modes.description: Colleagues, tasks, deadlines, problems, managers and leave.
modes.descriptionTamil: சக ஊழியர்கள், வேலைகள், காலக்கெடு, சிக்கல்கள், மேலாளர், விடுப்பு.

modes.label: Software Developer English
modes.description: C, Angular, TypeScript, JavaScript, Linux, MySQL, Git and more.
modes.descriptionTamil: C, Angular, TypeScript, JavaScript, Linux, MySQL, Git மற்றும் பல.

modes.label: Interview Practice
modes.description: A mock interview from self introduction to closing, in order.
modes.descriptionTamil: சுய அறிமுகம் முதல் முடிவு வரை வரிசையாக ஒரு மாதிரி நேர்காணல்.

modes.label: Telephone English
modes.description: Phone calls: office calls, appointments, wrong numbers, messages.
modes.descriptionTamil: தொலைபேசி அழைப்புகள்: அலுவலகம், அப்பாயிண்ட்மென்ட், தவறான எண், செய்திகள்.

modes.label: Travel English
modes.description: Airport, hotel, trains, directions, sightseeing and trip plans.
modes.descriptionTamil: விமான நிலையம், ஹோட்டல், ரயில், வழி கேட்டல், சுற்றுலா, பயணத் திட்டம்.

modes.label: Grammar Practice
modes.description: Lela teaches one grammar point, then asks you to use it.
modes.descriptionTamil: ஒரு இலக்கணப் பகுதியை லீலா விளக்கி, அதைப் பயன்படுத்தச் சொல்வாள்.

modes.label: Vocabulary Practice
modes.description: Learn a word, then say your own sentence using it.
modes.descriptionTamil: ஒரு சொல்லைக் கற்று, அதைப் பயன்படுத்தி உங்கள் சொந்த வாக்கியம் சொல்லுங்கள்.

modes.label: Advanced English Discussion
modes.description: Opinions, technology, career, goals, agreeing and disagreeing.
modes.descriptionTamil: கருத்துகள், தொழில்நுட்பம், தொழில் வளர்ச்சி, இலக்குகள், ஒப்புதல், மறுப்பு.

topics.title: Future with will and going to
keywords: future with will and going to

questions.text: What is your name?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பெயர் என்ன?
questions.example: My name is Priya.

questions.text: How old are you?
questions.tamil: உங்களுக்கு எத்தனை வயது?
questions.example: I am twenty-eight years old.

reactions.say: Thank you for sharing that.
reactions.ask: What is something you enjoy at this age?
reactions.askTamil: இந்த வயதில் உங்களுக்குப் பிடித்த ஒரு விஷயம் என்ன?

questions.text: How do you spell your name?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பெயரை எப்படி எழுத்துக் கூட்டுவீர்கள்?
questions.example: It is P, R, I, Y, A.

reactions.say: Thanks! Spelling names clearly is a useful skill.
reactions.ask: Do people often spell your name wrong?
reactions.askTamil: மக்கள் உங்கள் பெயரைத் தவறாக எழுதுவது உண்டா?

questions.text: Can you introduce yourself to me in a few short sentences?
questions.tamil: உங்களை என்னிடம் சில சிறிய வாக்கியங்களில் அறிமுகம் செய்து கொள்ள முடியுமா?
questions.example: I am Priya. I work as a software developer in Chennai. I like music and reading.

reactions.say: A good introduction! IT jobs are very popular.
reactions.ask: What do you enjoy most about your work?
reactions.askTamil: உங்கள் வேலையில் உங்களுக்கு மிகவும் பிடித்தது என்ன?

reactions.say: I see. Student life can be very busy.
reactions.ask: What are you studying at the moment?
reactions.askTamil: நீங்கள் இப்போது என்ன படிக்கிறீர்கள்?

questions.text: Does your name have a special meaning, or who chose it for you?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பெயருக்குச் சிறப்பான அர்த்தம் உள்ளதா, அல்லது அதை யார் தேர்ந்தெடுத்தார்கள்?
questions.example: My grandfather chose my name. It means light.

reactions.say: It is nice when a name comes from the family.
reactions.ask: Is there a family tradition for naming children?
reactions.askTamil: குழந்தைகளுக்குப் பெயர் வைக்க உங்கள் குடும்பத்தில் ஏதாவது பாரம்பரியம் உள்ளதா?

reactions.say: That sounds meaningful.

questions.text: When is your birthday, and how do you usually celebrate it?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பிறந்தநாள் எப்போது, அதை வழக்கமாக எப்படிக் கொண்டாடுவீர்கள்?
questions.example: My birthday is in March. I usually have dinner with my family.

reactions.say: Birthday parties sound fun!
A quiet family celebration is lovely.
Spending time with friends makes a day special.

questions.text: Imagine it is your first day with a new team. How would you introduce yourself professionally?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் புதிய குழுவில் முதல் நாள் என்று கற்பனை செய்யுங்கள். உங்களை எப்படித் தொழில்முறையாக அறிமுகம் செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: Hello everyone, I am Priya. I have three years of experience in web development, and I am happy to join this team.

reactions.say: Mentioning your experience is a strong start.
A positive tone makes a great first impression.

questions.text: Do you think a name is important for a person's identity? Why or why not?
questions.tamil: ஒருவரின் அடையாளத்திற்குப் பெயர் முக்கியமானது என்று நினைக்கிறீர்களா? ஏன்?
questions.example: Yes, I think so. A name is the first thing people know about us, and it connects us to our family.

reactions.say: That is an interesting point of view.
I see. That is a fair opinion.

questions.text: Some people use a short nickname at work. What do you think about nicknames in a professional setting?
questions.tamil: சிலர் அலுவலகத்தில் சுருக்கப் பெயரைப் பயன்படுத்துகிறார்கள். தொழில்முறைச் சூழலில் செல்லப் பெயர்கள் பற்றி என்ன நினைக்கிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I think nicknames are fine if everyone is comfortable. They can make the team feel friendly.

reactions.say: Good point. Comfort matters for everyone.
Yes, respect is important at work.

questions.text: Where are you from?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் எந்த ஊரைச் சேர்ந்தவர்?
questions.example: I am from Madurai.

reactions.say: Chennai is a big, busy city!
reactions.ask: What do you like most about Chennai?
reactions.askTamil: சென்னையில் உங்களுக்கு மிகவும் பிடித்தது என்ன?

reactions.say: Coimbatore is known for its pleasant weather.
reactions.ask: What is a nice place to visit around Coimbatore?
reactions.askTamil: கோயம்புத்தூரைச் சுற்றிப் பார்க்க ஒரு நல்ல இடம் எது?

reactions.say: Madurai has a very rich culture.
reactions.ask: What is the best time of year to visit Madurai?
reactions.askTamil: மதுரைக்குச் செல்ல ஆண்டின் சிறந்த நேரம் எது?

reactions.say: Village life is quite different from the city.
reactions.ask: What is the best part about growing up in a village?
reactions.askTamil: கிராமத்தில் வளர்வதில் சிறந்த பகுதி என்ன?

questions.text: Is your hometown big or small?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் சொந்த ஊர் பெரியதா, சிறியதா?
questions.example: It is a small town.

reactions.say: A small place often has a close community.
Big cities have many things going on.

questions.text: Do you still live in your hometown?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் இன்னும் உங்கள் சொந்த ஊரில் வசிக்கிறீர்களா?
questions.example: No, I live in Chennai now.

reactions.say: Living near your roots can be comforting.
I see. Many people move for work or study.
That is a popular city for IT jobs.

questions.text: What is your hometown famous for? Is there a special food or place?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் சொந்த ஊர் எதற்குப் புகழ்பெற்றது? சிறப்பான உணவு அல்லது இடம் உள்ளதா?
questions.example: My town is famous for its temple and for a sweet called halwa.

reactions.say: Temples are an important part of many towns.
That sounds tasty!
Natural places are lovely to visit.

questions.text: How do you travel between your hometown and the city where you work?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் சொந்த ஊருக்கும் நீங்கள் வேலை செய்யும் நகரத்துக்கும் இடையே எப்படிப் பயணம் செய்கிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I usually go by train. It takes about eight hours.

reactions.say: Trains are a comfortable way to travel.
Long bus trips can be tiring, but they are convenient.
That sounds like a quick way to go.

questions.text: What do you miss most about your hometown when you are away from it?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் வெளியே இருக்கும்போது உங்கள் சொந்த ஊரில் எதை மிகவும் இழக்கிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I miss my mother's cooking and the quiet evenings.

reactions.say: Home food is hard to replace!
Staying in touch with loved ones helps.
A calm place is something special.

questions.text: How has your hometown changed since you were a child, and do you think those changes are good?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் குழந்தையாக இருந்த காலத்திலிருந்து உங்கள் ஊர் எப்படி மாறியுள்ளது, அந்த மாற்றங்கள் நல்லவையா?
questions.example: There are more shops and better roads now. I think it is good, but traffic has also increased.

reactions.say: Growth can bring some problems too.
Development changes a place quickly.
Some places keep their charm for many years.

questions.text: Would you prefer to live in a village, a small town, or a big city? Please explain your reasons.
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் கிராமம், சிறிய நகரம் அல்லது பெரிய நகரத்தில் எங்கே வசிக்க விரும்புவீர்கள்? காரணங்களைக் கூறுங்கள்.
questions.example: I would prefer a small town. It is peaceful, but it still has good facilities and jobs.

reactions.say: Villages offer fresh air and a slow pace.
A small town can be a nice balance.
Big cities offer more job opportunities.

questions.text: If a foreign visitor came to your hometown for one day, what would you show them and why?
questions.tamil: ஒரு வெளிநாட்டுப் பயணி ஒரு நாள் உங்கள் ஊருக்கு வந்தால், எதைக் காட்டுவீர்கள், ஏன்?
questions.example: I would take them to the old temple and then to a local restaurant, so they can see our culture and taste our food.

reactions.say: Historic places tell a lot about a town.
Local food is a great way to know a culture.

questions.text: Do you have a big family?
questions.tamil: உங்களுக்குப் பெரிய குடும்பம் உள்ளதா?
questions.example: No, I have a small family.

reactions.say: A lively family sounds wonderful!
Every family size has its own good points.

questions.text: How many people are in your family?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் குடும்பத்தில் எத்தனை பேர் இருக்கிறார்கள்?
questions.example: There are four people in my family.

reactions.say: That is a nice family size.
That is a big family!

questions.text: Who do you live with?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் யாருடன் வசிக்கிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I live with my parents and my sister.

reactions.say: Living with parents can be comforting.
Living independently teaches many things.
I hope you enjoy your time together.

questions.text: Can you tell me a little about your parents and what they do?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பெற்றோர் பற்றியும் அவர்கள் என்ன செய்கிறார்கள் என்பதையும் சொல்ல முடியுமா?
questions.example: My father is a teacher and my mother takes care of our home.

reactions.say: That is a respectable profession.
That is a steady kind of job.

questions.text: Do you have any brothers or sisters, and are you close to them?
questions.tamil: உங்களுக்குச் சகோதரர்கள் அல்லது சகோதரிகள் இருக்கிறார்களா, அவர்களுடன் நெருக்கமாக இருக்கிறீர்களா?
questions.example: I have one younger brother. We are very close and we often talk on the phone.

reactions.say: A brother can be a great friend.
reactions.ask: What do you two like to do together?
reactions.askTamil: நீங்கள் இருவரும் சேர்ந்து என்ன செய்ய விரும்புவீர்கள்?

reactions.say: Sisters often share a special bond.
reactions.ask: What is your favourite memory with her?
reactions.askTamil: அவருடன் உங்கள் மிகப் பிடித்த நினைவு என்ன?

reactions.say: Being an only child has its own advantages.

questions.text: How often do you meet your relatives, and what do you usually do together?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் உறவினர்களை எவ்வளவு அடிக்கடி சந்திக்கிறீர்கள், சேர்ந்து என்ன செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: We meet during festivals. We cook together, eat, and talk for hours.

reactions.say: Festivals bring families together.
Busy lives can make it hard to meet.
Regular meetings keep the bond strong.

questions.text: How has the idea of a family changed in India over the last few decades?
questions.tamil: கடந்த சில பத்தாண்டுகளில் இந்தியாவில் குடும்பம் என்ற கருத்து எப்படி மாறியுள்ளது?
questions.example: I think families are smaller now, and many young people live far from their parents because of jobs.

reactions.say: Yes, nuclear families are becoming common.
Work does move many people far away.

questions.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of a joint family compared with a nuclear family?
questions.tamil: கூட்டுக் குடும்பத்தையும் தனிக் குடும்பத்தையும் ஒப்பிடும்போது அதன் நன்மைகள், தீமைகள் என்ன?
questions.example: A joint family gives emotional support and shared work, but there is less privacy.

reactions.say: Privacy is a fair point.
Support from family is valuable.

questions.text: How do you balance your career goals with your responsibilities to your family?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் தொழில் இலக்குகளையும் குடும்பப் பொறுப்புகளையும் எப்படிச் சமநிலைப்படுத்துகிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I plan my time carefully. I give full attention to work during office hours, and evenings are for my family.

reactions.say: Good planning really helps.
It is not easy for many people.

questions.text: What did you study?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் என்ன படித்தீர்கள்?
questions.example: I studied computer science.

reactions.say: Computer studies are a great base for an IT career.
reactions.ask: Which part of it did you enjoy most?
reactions.askTamil: அதில் எந்தப் பகுதி உங்களுக்கு மிகவும் பிடித்தது?

reactions.say: That is a useful subject area.

questions.text: Did you like your school days?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் பள்ளி நாட்கள் உங்களுக்குப் பிடித்திருந்தனவா?
questions.example: Yes, I did. I had many good friends.

reactions.say: School days often leave warm memories.
I see. Not everyone enjoys school.
People make school memorable.

questions.text: What was your favourite subject?
questions.tamil: உங்களுக்குப் பிடித்த பாடம் எது?
questions.example: My favourite subject was maths.

reactions.say: Maths helps a lot in programming.
Languages are a lovely subject.
Science makes us curious about the world.
That is an interesting subject.

questions.text: Which college or university did you attend, and what was your degree about?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் எந்தக் கல்லூரி அல்லது பல்கலைக்கழகத்தில் படித்தீர்கள், உங்கள் பட்டம் எதைப் பற்றியது?
questions.example: I studied at an engineering college in Coimbatore. My degree was in information technology.

reactions.say: Engineering college life is usually very busy.
University life can be very exciting.
A good field for today's job market.

questions.text: What was the most difficult subject for you, and how did you deal with it?
questions.tamil: உங்களுக்கு மிகக் கடினமான பாடம் எது, அதை எப்படிச் சமாளித்தீர்கள்?
questions.example: Physics was difficult for me. I asked my friends for help and practised every day.

reactions.say: Many students find that subject challenging.
Asking for help is a smart habit.
Regular practice makes a big difference.

questions.text: Did you do any projects or internships during your studies, and what did you learn?
questions.tamil: படிக்கும் காலத்தில் ஏதாவது திட்டங்கள் அல்லது இன்டர்ன்ஷிப் செய்தீர்களா, அதில் என்ன கற்றீர்கள்?
questions.example: Yes, I did a small web project in my final year. I learned how a team works together.

reactions.say: Projects are the best way to learn.
An internship gives real work experience.
That is okay. You can learn a lot on the job too.

reactions.say: Giving a clear number of days is helpful.
A polite tone makes people listen.

questions.text: What tools or habits help you remember your deadlines?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் டெட்லைன்களை நினைவில் வைத்துக்கொள்ள என்ன கருவிகள் அல்லது பழக்கங்கள் உதவுகின்றன?
questions.example: I keep a to-do list and set calendar reminders a day before every due date.

reactions.say: Reminders save many people!
A written list clears the mind.
Tracking tools are very useful for teams.

questions.text: How do you decide which tasks to do first when you have several deadlines at the same time?
questions.tamil: ஒரே நேரத்தில் பல டெட்லைன்கள் இருக்கும்போது எந்த வேலையை முதலில் செய்வது என்று எப்படி முடிவு செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I look at the urgency and the business impact, and I discuss the order with my manager if needed.

reactions.say: Urgent and important are not always the same.
Customer impact is a strong guide.
Checking with the manager avoids surprises.

questions.text: What are the dangers of always working under pressure to meet tight deadlines?
questions.tamil: எப்போதும் இறுக்கமான டெட்லைன்களை அடைய அழுத்தத்தில் வேலை செய்வதால் என்ன ஆபத்துகள் உள்ளன?
questions.example: It can cause burnout and more mistakes, and the quality of the product may go down.

reactions.say: Looking after yourself matters in a long career.
Rushing often creates more bugs.
Rest is part of good work.

questions.text: How can a team set more realistic deadlines in the first place?
questions.tamil: ஒரு குழு முதலிலேயே மேலும் யதார்த்தமான டெட்லைன்களை எப்படி நிர்ணயிக்கலாம்?
questions.example: They can estimate in small pieces, add some buffer time, and review past projects to learn how long things really took.

reactions.say: Buffer time is very sensible.
Estimating small pieces is more accurate.
Learning from past work is the best guide.

questions.text: Have you ever found a problem at work?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் எப்போதாவது வேலையில் ஒரு பிரச்சனையை கண்டுபிடித்திருக்கிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I found a bug last week.

reactions.say: Finding problems early is a useful skill.
Good! Hopefully your work stays smooth.

questions.text: Who do you tell when something goes wrong?
questions.tamil: ஏதாவது தவறாகப் போனால் யாரிடம் சொல்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I tell my team lead.

reactions.say: Telling the right person quickly is important.
The support team can often help fast.

questions.text: Is the server working today?
questions.tamil: இன்று சர்வர் வேலை செய்கிறதா?
questions.example: No, the server is down.

reactions.say: That sounds stressful. I hope it is fixed soon.
Good, no trouble today then.

questions.text: How do you describe a problem clearly in an email to the support team?
questions.tamil: சப்போர்ட் குழுவுக்கு அனுப்பும் மின்னஞ்சலில் ஒரு பிரச்சனையை தெளிவாக எப்படி விவரிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I write what happened, when it started, the error message, and the steps to repeat the issue.

reactions.say: The exact error message is very valuable.
Clear steps help others see the same problem.
A screenshot says more than many words.

questions.text: You notice a mistake in your colleague's work. How do you tell them politely?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் சக ஊழியரின் வேலையில் ஒரு தவறை கவனிக்கிறீர்கள். அவரிடம் நாகரிகமாக எப்படி சொல்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would say, "I think there may be a small issue here. Can we check it together?"

reactions.say: Working together keeps things friendly.
Speaking privately is thoughtful.
Soft language keeps the talk positive.

questions.text: Tell me about a time when you made a mistake at work. How did you report it?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் வேலையில் ஒரு தவறு செய்த சந்தர்ப்பத்தைப் பற்றி சொல்லுங்கள். அதை எப்படி தெரிவித்தீர்கள்?
questions.example: Once I deleted a file by mistake, so I told my lead immediately and we restored it from the backup.

reactions.say: Backups really save the day!
Honesty and speed are the best approach.
Everyone makes mistakes. What matters is how we handle them.

questions.text: Why is it important to report small problems early, before they become big ones?
questions.tamil: சிறிய பிரச்சனைகளை பெரியதாக மாறும் முன் ஏன் சீக்கிரமே தெரிவிப்பது முக்கியம்?
questions.example: Small issues are cheaper to fix, and early reports stop the same problem from spreading to other areas.

reactions.say: Early fixing really does save money.
Problems do tend to grow quietly.
Honest reporting builds team trust.

questions.text: How do you report a serious problem to a senior manager without sounding like you are blaming anyone?
questions.tamil: யாரையும் குற்றம் சாட்டுவது போல் ஒலிக்காமல், ஒரு பெரிய பிரச்சனையை மூத்த மேனேஜரிடம் எப்படி தெரிவிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I focus on facts and impact, describe what we know so far, and suggest the next steps instead of naming people.

reactions.say: Facts keep the conversation calm.
Avoiding blame helps people share information freely.
Offering next steps shows ownership.

questions.text: What is a blame-free culture, and do you think it helps teams learn from failures?
questions.tamil: பழி சுமத்தாத கலாச்சாரம் என்றால் என்ன? தோல்விகளிலிருந்து குழுக்கள் கற்க அது உதவுகிறது என்று நினைக்கிறீர்களா?
questions.example: It means people discuss failures openly without fear of punishment, so the team can find root causes and improve.

reactions.say: Finding the root cause is the real goal.
Fear makes people hide problems.
Learning from failure is a mark of mature teams.

questions.text: Do you like your manager?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் மேனேஜரை உங்களுக்குப் பிடிக்குமா?
questions.example: Yes, my manager is very kind.

reactions.say: It is lovely to have a supportive manager!
I see. Every manager has a different style.

questions.text: How often do you meet your manager?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் மேனேஜரை எவ்வளவு அடிக்கடி சந்திப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: We meet once a week.

reactions.say: Daily meetings keep everything fresh.
A weekly meeting is a good rhythm.
A monthly meeting gives you time to prepare.
I see. Maybe you can ask for a regular time.

questions.text: What does your manager ask you every day?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் மேனேஜர் தினமும் உங்களிடம் என்ன கேட்பார்?
questions.example: He asks about my work status.

reactions.say: Updates keep everyone informed.
Managers always like clear answers.
That means he trusts you to work independently.

questions.text: How would you describe your manager's way of working to a friend?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் மேனேஜரின் வேலை செய்யும் விதத்தை ஒரு நண்பருக்கு எப்படி விவரிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: He is calm and organised, and he gives clear instructions, so it is easy to work with him.

reactions.say: A calm manager makes work easier.
Strict managers can help people grow too.
Clear instructions are a big help.

questions.text: How do you ask your manager for feedback on your work?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் வேலையைப் பற்றிய கருத்தை உங்கள் மேனேஜரிடம் எப்படி கேட்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I ask, "Could you please tell me what I can improve in my work?" after finishing a task.

reactions.say: Asking how to improve shows a growth mindset.
Regular feedback is the fastest way to grow.
Asking right after a task is a smart timing.

questions.text: What would you do if you disagreed with a decision your manager made?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் மேனேஜர் எடுத்த முடிவில் உங்களுக்கு உடன்பாடு இல்லையென்றால் என்ன செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would wait for a private moment and respectfully explain my concern with some reasons.

reactions.say: A private chat is a respectful approach.
Giving reasons is much stronger than just opinions.
Accepting the final decision is also part of teamwork.

questions.text: What qualities make a good manager, in your opinion?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் கருத்தில் ஒரு நல்ல மேனேஜரை உருவாக்கும் குணங்கள் என்ன?
questions.example: A good manager listens, gives clear direction, supports the team in difficult times and recognises good work.

reactions.say: Listening is a rare and valuable skill.
Support builds loyalty in a team.
Direction helps people feel confident.
A little appreciation goes a long way.

questions.text: How do you build trust with a manager who is new to your team?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் குழுவுக்கு புதிதாக வந்த மேனேஜருடன் நம்பிக்கையை எப்படி உருவாக்குவீர்கள்?

reactions.say: Honesty is the foundation of trust.
Keeping promises builds a strong reputation.
Sharing context saves a new manager a lot of time.

questions.tamil: எல்லாவற்றிலும் தலையிடும் மேனேஜருக்கும் சுதந்திரம் தரும் மேனேஜருக்கும் என்ன வேறுபாடு? எந்த பாணியை விரும்புவீர்கள்?

reactions.say: Micromanagement can make people feel stressed.
Freedom brings responsibility with it.

questions.text: Do you take leave often?

reactions.say: Informing the right person is polite.

questions.text: How do you ask your manager for a day off for a family function?
questions.tamil: ஒரு குடும்ப நிகழ்ச்சிக்காக ஒரு நாள் விடுப்பு கேட்பதை உங்கள் மேனேஜரிடம் எப்படி கேட்பீர்கள்?

reactions.say: Family functions are important occasions in India.
Polite words always help.

questions.text: What do you do to make sure your work is covered while you are on leave?

reactions.say: A handover note is very professional.
A backup person gives peace of mind.
Writing it down avoids confusion.

questions.text: What would you say in an email to inform your team that you will be on leave next week?
questions.tamil: அடுத்த வாரம் நீங்கள் விடுப்பில் இருப்பீர்கள் என்று உங்கள் குழுவுக்கு தெரிவிக்கும் மின்னஞ்சலில் என்ன எழுதுவீர்கள்?

reactions.say: Naming a contact person is very helpful.
Clear dates avoid confusion.
Mentioning your return date is thoughtful.

questions.text: What is the difference between casual leave, sick leave and earned leave? How do you decide which to take?
questions.tamil: கேஷுவல் லீவ், சிக் லீவ், எர்ன்ட் லீவ் ஆகியவற்றுக்கு என்ன வேறுபாடு? எதை எடுப்பது என்று எப்படி தீர்மானிப்பீர்கள்?

questions.example: The team can plan early with a shared leave calendar, rotate responsibilities, and avoid big releases in that period.

reactions.say: A shared calendar makes planning much easier.
Sharing the load keeps things fair.
Avoiding big releases is a smart move.
Festival times are special, and teams like to enjoy them.

questions.text: Do you think work-life balance is important for productivity? Explain your view.
questions.tamil: வேலை-வாழ்க்கை சமநிலை உற்பத்தித்திறனுக்கு முக்கியம் என்று நினைக்கிறீர்களா? உங்கள் கருத்தை விளக்குங்கள்.
questions.example: Yes, because rested people think better and make fewer mistakes, so time off actually improves the quality of work.

reactions.say: Rest is a real part of productivity.
Looking after health helps long-term performance.
Time for family and hobbies recharges people.
Many teams are now thinking about this seriously.

questions.text: Do you write programs in C?

reactions.say: C is a classic language. Many people start with it!

questions.example: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable.

questions.tamil: C-யில் function என்ன செய்கிறது? நாம் ஏன் functions பயன்படுத்துகிறோம்?
questions.example: A function is a block of code that does one job. We use it to avoid repeating code.

reactions.say: Functions keep programs tidy.

Parameters make a function flexible.
Return values pass results back to the caller.

questions.text: Explain how malloc and free work, and what can go wrong if you use them carelessly.
questions.tamil: malloc மற்றும் free எப்படி வேலை செய்கின்றன, கவனக்குறைவாக பயன்படுத்தினால் என்ன தவறாகலாம் என்பதை விளக்குங்கள்.
questions.example: Malloc reserves memory on the heap and free releases it. If I forget to free, there is a memory leak.

Those errors are the stuff of many debugging nights!

questions.tamil: ஒரு function-க்கு மதிப்பை அனுப்புவதற்கும் pointer-ஐ அனுப்புவதற்கும் என்ன வேறுபாடு? எப்போது எதை தேர்ந்தெடுப்பீர்கள்?

questions.text: How do you share data between two Angular components?
questions.tamil: இரண்டு Angular components-க்கு இடையே data-வை எப்படி பகிர்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: A parent can pass data to a child with an input, and the child can send events back with an output.

reactions.say: Input is the usual way from parent to child.
Outputs send events up to the parent.
A shared service is also a popular choice.
Observables are handy for sharing live data.

questions.text: What is a service in Angular, and why do we use it?
questions.tamil: Angular-இல் service என்றால் என்ன? நாம் ஏன் அதைப் பயன்படுத்துகிறோம்?
questions.example: A service holds shared logic, like calling an API, so many components can use the same code.

reactions.say: Services keep components clean.
Dependency injection is a core Angular idea.
Calling the API from a service is a good practice.

questions.text: What is routing in Angular, and how do you move from one page to another?
questions.tamil: Angular-இல் routing என்றால் என்ன? ஒரு பக்கத்திலிருந்து மற்றொரு பக்கத்துக்கு எப்படி செல்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: Routing maps a URL to a component. I use a routerLink or the router to navigate between pages.

reactions.say: The router makes a single-page app feel like many pages.
Each URL points to one component.
Guards are useful to protect pages.
Lazy loading makes the first load faster.

questions.text: What is an observable in Angular, and how is it different from a promise?
questions.tamil: Angular-இல் observable என்றால் என்ன? அது promise-இலிருந்து எப்படி வேறுபடுகிறது?
questions.example: An observable can send many values over time and can be cancelled, but a promise gives one value only.

reactions.say: RxJS can feel big at first, but it is powerful.
A promise is simpler for a single result.
Remember to unsubscribe to avoid memory leaks!
Streams of data are the heart of reactive code.

questions.text: How do you improve the performance of a slow Angular application?
questions.tamil: மெதுவாக இயங்கும் Angular பயன்பாட்டின் செயல்திறனை எப்படி மேம்படுத்துவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use lazy loading, the OnPush strategy, trackBy in lists, and I avoid heavy work inside templates.

reactions.say: Lazy loading reduces the first load time.
Change detection tuning can give big gains.
Rendering long lists wisely makes a difference.
Smaller bundles load faster.

questions.text: How do you organise a large Angular project so that it stays easy to maintain as the team grows?
questions.tamil: குழு வளரும்போதும் எளிதில் பராமரிக்கும் வகையில் ஒரு பெரிய Angular ப்ராஜெக்டை எப்படி ஒழுங்கமைப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I split it into feature modules, keep shared code in one place, follow naming rules, and write tests for services.

reactions.say: Feature-based structure keeps things clear.
A shared area avoids duplicate code.
Tests protect a growing codebase.
Common rules help everyone read each other's code.

questions.text: What is TypeScript?
questions.tamil: TypeScript என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: TypeScript is JavaScript with types.

reactions.say: Short and correct!
Yes, it is a superset of JavaScript.

questions.text: Why do you use TypeScript?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் ஏன் TypeScript பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: It shows mistakes before I run the code.

reactions.say: Catching errors early saves a lot of time.
Types are like a safety net.
Editor support is a big benefit too.

questions.text: Name two basic types in TypeScript.
questions.tamil: TypeScript-இல் இரண்டு அடிப்படை type-களின் பெயர்களை சொல்லுங்கள்.
questions.example: String and number are two basic types.

reactions.say: Good! Those are the basic ones.
Those are common too.

questions.text: What is an interface in TypeScript, and when would you use it?
questions.tamil: TypeScript-இல் interface என்றால் என்ன? எப்போது அதைப் பயன்படுத்துவீர்கள்?
questions.example: An interface describes the shape of an object. I use it for data from an API.

reactions.say: Interfaces describe objects nicely.
Describing the shape keeps data predictable.
Typing API data prevents many bugs.

questions.text: What is the difference between let, const and var?
questions.tamil: let, const, var ஆகியவற்றுக்கு இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: Const cannot be reassigned, let can change, and var is the old style with function scope.

reactions.say: Const is a good default choice.
Let has block scope, which is easier to reason about.
Most teams avoid var today.

questions.text: What does the type any mean, and why do many developers avoid it?
questions.tamil: any type என்றால் என்ன? பல developers அதை ஏன் தவிர்க்கிறார்கள்?
questions.example: Any turns off type checking for that value, so we lose the safety that TypeScript gives us.

reactions.say: Using any too much removes the main benefit.
Unknown or generics are safer options.
Type safety is the whole point.

questions.text: How do generics work in TypeScript? Give an example of where they are useful.
questions.tamil: TypeScript-இல் generics எப்படி வேலை செய்கின்றன? அவை பயன்படும் ஒரு உதாரணம் சொல்லுங்கள்.
questions.example: Generics let a function or class work with many types and keep type safety, for example a list of any item type.

reactions.say: Generics are great for reusable code.
Typed collections are a classic example.
Reusable and safe is a nice combination.
They work in functions, classes and interfaces.

questions.text: What are the trade-offs of using TypeScript instead of plain JavaScript in a small project?
questions.tamil: ஒரு சிறிய ப்ராஜெக்டில் சாதாரண JavaScript-க்கு பதிலாக TypeScript பயன்படுத்துவதன் நன்மை தீமைகள் என்ன?
questions.example: TypeScript adds setup and a learning curve, but it gives better tooling and fewer runtime bugs, even in small projects.

reactions.say: Extra setup is a fair cost.
The learning curve is real for new people.
Good tooling is a big benefit.
Fewer runtime surprises is nice.

questions.text: How would you gradually move an existing JavaScript project to TypeScript?
questions.tamil: ஏற்கனவே உள்ள ஒரு JavaScript ப்ராஜெக்டை படிப்படியாக TypeScript-க்கு எப்படி மாற்றுவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would allow both file types, rename files one by one, start with loose settings, and make the rules stricter over time.

reactions.say: Small steps lower the risk.
Tightening the config over time is a good plan.
Many teams follow that exact path.
Tests help you move safely.

questions.text: Do you use JavaScript in your work?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் உங்கள் வேலையில் JavaScript பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I use JavaScript for the web pages.

reactions.say: JavaScript is everywhere on the web!
That is fine. Many roles do not need it.

questions.text: What is a function in JavaScript?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் function என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A function is a block of code that does a task.

reactions.say: Functions are the building blocks of JavaScript.
A function can be used again and again.

questions.text: What is an array in JavaScript?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் array என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: An array is a list of values.

reactions.say: Arrays are used in almost every project.
Remember that the index starts from zero.

questions.text: What is a promise in JavaScript, and why do we need it?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் promise என்றால் என்ன? நமக்கு ஏன் அது தேவை?
questions.example: A promise represents a result that will come later, like data from a server, so the code does not freeze while waiting.

reactions.say: Promises make waiting tasks easier to handle.
Asynchronous code is a key idea in JavaScript.
Those keywords are used all the time.
Server calls are the usual example.

questions.text: What is the difference between double equals and triple equals in JavaScript?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் double equals மற்றும் triple equals இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: Double equals converts types before comparing, but triple equals compares both the value and the type.

reactions.say: Most developers prefer the strict one.
Type conversion can create surprising results.
Yes, that is where the confusion comes from.

questions.text: How do you use map and filter on an array? Give a simple example.
questions.tamil: ஒரு array-வில் map மற்றும் filter-ஐ எப்படி பயன்படுத்துவீர்கள்? ஒரு எளிய உதாரணம் சொல்லுங்கள்.
questions.example: Map changes every item to make a new array, and filter keeps only the items that match a condition.

reactions.say: Map is perfect for transforming data.
Filter is great for selecting what you need.
Those array helpers are very useful too.
Not changing the original is a nice habit.

questions.text: Explain async and await. How do they make asynchronous code easier to read?
questions.tamil: async மற்றும் await பற்றி விளக்குங்கள். அவை asynchronous code-ஐ படிக்க எப்படி எளிதாக்குகின்றன?
questions.example: Await pauses a function until a promise finishes, so asynchronous code looks like normal step-by-step code.

reactions.say: Async and await really clean up the code.
Yes, they are built on promises.
Do not forget error handling with try and catch.
Callback hell is a thing of the past, thankfully.

questions.text: What is a closure in JavaScript? Where have you seen it used in real projects?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் closure என்றால் என்ன? உண்மையான ப்ராஜெக்ட்களில் அது எங்கே பயன்படுத்தப்படுவதை பார்த்திருக்கிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: A closure is a function that remembers the variables from the place where it was created, even after that place has finished.

reactions.say: Closures are a favourite interview topic!
Scope is the heart of the idea.
Counters and event handlers are common examples.

questions.text: How does the event loop work in JavaScript, and why does it matter for performance?
questions.tamil: JavaScript-இல் event loop எப்படி வேலை செய்கிறது? அது செயல்திறனுக்கு ஏன் முக்கியம்?
questions.example: JavaScript runs one task at a time, and the event loop picks the next task from a queue, so heavy work can block the page.

reactions.say: The event loop is a tricky but important topic.
Yes, JavaScript is single threaded.
Blocking the main thread makes pages feel slow.
Workers and async work help avoid that.

questions.text: What is HTML used for?
questions.tamil: HTML எதற்காக பயன்படுத்தப்படுகிறது?
questions.example: HTML is used to build the structure of a web page.

reactions.say: Right, it is the skeleton of every page.
Tags are the pieces that form the page.

questions.text: What is CSS used for?
questions.tamil: CSS எதற்காக பயன்படுத்தப்படுகிறது?
questions.example: CSS is used to style the page, like colours and fonts.

reactions.say: CSS makes the web look nice.
Colours and fonts change the whole feel of a page.

questions.text: Which HTML tags do you use most?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் அதிகமாக பயன்படுத்தும் HTML tags எவை?
questions.example: I use div, p and a tags the most.

reactions.say: Containers are used everywhere.
Images make pages interesting.
Forms and buttons make pages interactive.
Links are the core of the web!

questions.text: How do you centre an element on a web page using CSS?
questions.tamil: CSS பயன்படுத்தி ஒரு element-ஐ பக்கத்தின் நடுவில் எப்படி வைப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use flexbox with justify-content and align-items set to center.

reactions.say: Flexbox makes centring so much easier.
Grid is also a neat way to centre.
Margin auto is the classic method.
Centring is a famous CSS struggle!

questions.text: What is the difference between a class and an id in CSS?
questions.tamil: CSS-இல் class மற்றும் id இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: An id must be unique on a page, but a class can be used on many elements.

reactions.say: Classes are the most common choice for styling.
Ids are for single, special elements.
Selectors are the heart of CSS.

questions.text: How do you make a web page look good on both mobile and desktop?
questions.tamil: ஒரு வலைப்பக்கம் மொபைல் மற்றும் டெஸ்க்டாப் இரண்டிலும் நன்றாகத் தெரிய எப்படி செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use responsive design with media queries, flexible units like percentages, and I test on different screen sizes.

reactions.say: Responsive design is essential today.
Most users are on mobile phones now.
Flexible layouts adapt very well.
Browser dev tools make testing easy.

questions.text: Explain the CSS box model. Why is it important when you design a layout?
questions.tamil: CSS box model-ஐ விளக்குங்கள். ஒரு layout வடிவமைக்கும்போது அது ஏன் முக்கியம்?
questions.example: Every element is a box with content, padding, border and margin. Knowing this helps me control spacing and size.

reactions.say: Those layers are easy to mix up!
The box model explains many layout surprises.
Sizes and spacing depend on it.

questions.text: What are the advantages of CSS Grid and Flexbox? How do you decide which to use?
questions.tamil: CSS Grid மற்றும் Flexbox-இன் நன்மைகள் என்ன? எதை பயன்படுத்துவது என்று எப்படி முடிவு செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: Flexbox is best for one direction, like a row or column, while Grid is better for two-dimensional layouts. I often combine them.

reactions.say: Flexbox is great for aligning items.
Grid shines in full page layouts.
Thinking in rows and columns helps choose.
Using both is very common.

questions.text: How do you make a website accessible for people who use screen readers or have low vision?
questions.tamil: திரை வாசிப்பான்களைப் பயன்படுத்துபவர்கள் அல்லது குறைந்த பார்வை உள்ளவர்களுக்கு ஒரு வலைத்தளத்தை எப்படி அணுகக்கூடியதாக மாற்றுவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use semantic HTML, add alt text to images, keep good colour contrast, and make sure everything works with a keyboard.

reactions.say: Semantic HTML is the best first step.
Good contrast helps many users.
Keyboard support is very important.
Testing with a screen reader teaches a lot.

questions.text: Do you use Linux at work?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் வேலையில் Linux பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I use Linux on our servers.

reactions.say: Linux runs a huge part of the internet!

questions.text: Which Linux command do you use most?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் அதிகமாக பயன்படுத்தும் Linux command எது?
questions.example: I use the ls command the most.

reactions.say: Basic commands are used all the time.
Those are great search tools.
Good for reading files and logs.
Careful with sudo!

questions.text: What does the cd command do?
questions.tamil: cd command என்ன செய்கிறது?
questions.example: It changes the current directory.

reactions.say: Correct! Moving around is the first skill.
Yes, it takes you to another folder.

questions.text: How do you see the last lines of a log file, and watch new lines as they appear?
questions.tamil: ஒரு log file-இன் கடைசி வரிகளை எப்படி பார்ப்பீர்கள், புதிய வரிகள் வரும்போது எப்படி கவனிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use the tail command with the minus f option, and it keeps showing new lines as they are written.

reactions.say: Tail is a favourite of every support engineer.
Reading logs is a daily task for many.
Those also help with reading files.
Live logs make debugging much faster.

questions.text: What is the difference between a file and a directory in Linux, and how do you create each one?
questions.tamil: Linux-இல் file மற்றும் directory இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு? ஒவ்வொன்றையும் எப்படி உருவாக்குவீர்கள்?
questions.example: A file stores data, and a directory holds files. I use touch for a file and mkdir for a directory.

reactions.say: Simple and useful commands.
Files are the base of everything in Linux.
Folders keep things organised.

questions.text: What does chmod do, and why are file permissions important?
questions.tamil: chmod என்ன செய்கிறது? file permissions ஏன் முக்கியம்?
questions.example: Chmod changes who can read, write or run a file. It keeps files safe from the wrong users.

reactions.say: Permissions are a core Linux idea.
Read, write and execute are the three basics.
Good permissions protect a system.
Be careful with very open permissions!

questions.text: How do you find out which process is using too much CPU or memory on a Linux server, and what do you do next?
questions.tamil: ஒரு Linux server-இல் எந்த process அதிக CPU அல்லது memory பயன்படுத்துகிறது என்பதை எப்படி கண்டுபிடிப்பீர்கள், அடுத்து என்ன செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I check with top or htop, find the process id, look at its logs, and restart or stop it carefully if it is stuck.

reactions.say: Those tools give a quick picture.
Understanding processes is key on servers.
Kill carefully, and check the impact first.
Resource problems can be tricky to trace.

questions.text: What is the difference between grep, find and awk? Explain when you would use each.
questions.tamil: grep, find, awk ஆகியவற்றுக்கு என்ன வேறுபாடு? ஒவ்வொன்றையும் எப்போது பயன்படுத்துவீர்கள்?
questions.example: Grep searches text inside files, find searches for files by name or date, and awk processes columns of text.

reactions.say: Grep is a developer's best friend.
Find is great for locating files.
Awk and sed make text processing powerful.
Combining commands with pipes is the Linux spirit.

questions.text: How would you automate a daily task on a Linux server, such as taking a backup, and how would you make sure it keeps working?
questions.tamil: ஒரு Linux server-இல் backup எடுப்பது போன்ற தினசரி வேலையை எப்படி தானியக்கமாக்குவீர்கள், அது தொடர்ந்து சரியாக ஓடுவதை எப்படி உறுதி செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would write a shell script, schedule it with cron, log the output, and send an alert if it fails.

reactions.say: Cron is the classic Linux scheduler.
Shell scripts automate so much work.
Alerts help you notice failures quickly.
Logging is essential for automated jobs.

questions.text: Do you use MySQL in your work?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் உங்கள் வேலையில் MySQL பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I use MySQL for our application data.

reactions.say: MySQL is used in many companies.
Other databases are popular too.

questions.text: What is a database?
questions.tamil: Database என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A database is a place to store data in an organised way.

reactions.say: Right, it keeps data safe and tidy.
Tables are where the rows live.

questions.text: What is a table in MySQL?
questions.tamil: MySQL-இல் table என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A table stores data in rows and columns.

reactions.say: A table is just like a spreadsheet.
Each row is one record.

questions.text: How do you get all employees who work in the Chennai office using SQL? Explain the query.
questions.tamil: SQL பயன்படுத்தி சென்னை அலுவலகத்தில் வேலை செய்யும் அனைத்து ஊழியர்களையும் எப்படி பெறுவீர்கள்? அந்த query-ஐ விளக்குங்கள்.
questions.example: I use SELECT star FROM employees WHERE city equals Chennai. The WHERE clause filters the rows.

reactions.say: Select is the most used SQL word.
WHERE helps you narrow the result.
Always name the table you read from.

questions.text: What is a primary key, and why does every table need one?
questions.tamil: primary key என்றால் என்ன? ஒவ்வொரு table-க்கும் அது ஏன் தேவை?
questions.example: A primary key is a unique value for each row, like an employee id, so we can find one row exactly.

reactions.say: Primary keys keep records unique.
Unique ids are the base of good design.
Auto increment is a handy feature.

questions.text: What is the difference between INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE?
questions.tamil: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ஆகியவற்றுக்கு இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: Insert adds a new row, update changes an existing row, and delete removes a row.

reactions.say: Insert creates new records.
Always use WHERE with update!
Delete without WHERE is a famous mistake.

questions.text: Explain what a JOIN is. What is the difference between an inner join and a left join?
questions.tamil: JOIN என்றால் என்ன என்பதை விளக்குங்கள். inner join மற்றும் left join இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: A join combines rows from two tables. An inner join returns only matching rows, but a left join also keeps all rows from the left table.

reactions.say: Joins are the heart of relational databases.
Inner join gives only the matches.
Left join keeps unmatched left rows with nulls.
Foreign keys connect the tables.

questions.text: What is an index in a database, and what are the trade-offs of adding many indexes?
questions.tamil: database-இல் index என்றால் என்ன? அதிக indexes சேர்ப்பதன் நன்மை தீமைகள் என்ன?
questions.example: An index makes searching faster, like the index of a book, but it uses extra space and makes writes slower.

reactions.say: Indexes can improve speed a lot.
Faster reads are the big benefit.
More indexes mean more work on every write.
EXPLAIN is a good tool for checking queries.

questions.text: How do you investigate and fix a slow query in MySQL?
questions.tamil: MySQL-இல் மெதுவாக இயங்கும் query-ஐ எப்படி ஆராய்ந்து சரிசெய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I run EXPLAIN to see how the query executes, add a suitable index, avoid selecting unnecessary columns, and test again.

reactions.say: EXPLAIN shows the execution plan clearly.
The right index often fixes the problem.
Joins on unindexed columns are a common cause.
Fetching less data helps too.

questions.text: Do you find many bugs in your code?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் code-இல் நிறைய bugs கிடைக்குமா?
questions.example: Yes, I find some bugs every day.

reactions.say: Bugs are a normal part of programming!
That is impressive, or maybe your tests are great!

questions.text: What is a bug?
questions.tamil: bug என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A bug is a mistake in a program.

reactions.say: Simple and clear.
Yes, it makes the program behave in a wrong way.

questions.text: What do you do first when your code fails?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் code தோல்வியடைந்தால் முதலில் என்ன செய்வீர்கள்?
questions.example: I read the error message first.

reactions.say: Reading the error message is the best first step.
Searching the message is a popular habit.
Sometimes a restart really does help!

questions.text: How do you use a debugger or breakpoints to find a problem in your code?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் code-இல் பிரச்சனையை கண்டுபிடிக்க debugger அல்லது breakpoints-ஐ எப்படி பயன்படுத்துவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I put a breakpoint near the problem, run the code, and check the variable values step by step.

reactions.say: Breakpoints show exactly what is happening.
Stepping through code teaches a lot.
Watching values is the key idea.

questions.text: What is the difference between a syntax error and a logic error?
questions.tamil: syntax error மற்றும் logic error இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: A syntax error breaks the language rules, so the code will not run. A logic error runs, but gives the wrong result.

reactions.say: Syntax errors are usually easy to see.
Logic errors are harder because nothing crashes.
Runtime errors appear while the program runs.

questions.text: How do you use log messages to understand what your program is doing?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் நிரல் என்ன செய்கிறது என்பதை புரிந்துகொள்ள log messages-ஐ எப்படி பயன்படுத்துவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I add log lines at important steps, with useful details like ids, so I can follow the flow later.

reactions.say: Good logs are a developer's best friend.
Print statements are a quick first tool.
Log levels keep the output tidy.

questions.text: How do you find the root cause of a bug that happens only in production and never on your machine?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் கணினியில் ஒருபோதும் நடக்காமல், production-இல் மட்டுமே நடக்கும் bug-இன் மூல காரணத்தை எப்படி கண்டுபிடிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I compare the environments, study the production logs, try to reproduce the case with similar data, and then make a small safe change.

reactions.say: Production logs are often the best clue.
Differences in environment or data cause many such bugs.
Reproducing it is half of the fix.
Monitoring tools give valuable hints.

questions.text: How do you stop a bug from coming back after you fix it?
questions.tamil: ஒரு bug-ஐ சரிசெய்த பிறகு அது மீண்டும் வராமல் எப்படி தடுப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I write a test that fails before the fix and passes after it, and I review similar places in the code.

reactions.say: A regression test is a strong protection.
Code reviews catch repeat mistakes.
Writing down the lesson helps the team.
Fixing the root cause matters most.

questions.text: Describe your step-by-step approach when you are stuck on a problem for hours. What helps you move forward?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் பல மணி நேரம் ஒரு பிரச்சனையில் சிக்கிக்கொண்டால் உங்கள் படிப்படியான அணுகுமுறையை விவரியுங்கள். முன்னேற உங்களுக்கு எது உதவுகிறது?
questions.example: I take a short break, explain the problem aloud to a colleague, shrink it to the smallest example, and then check my assumptions.

reactions.say: A short break often brings a fresh view.
Explaining aloud really works. People call it rubber duck debugging!
Another pair of eyes can solve it quickly.
A minimal example makes the cause clear.

questions.text: What is an API?
questions.tamil: API என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: An API lets two programs talk to each other.

reactions.say: Nice way to say it!
APIs connect software pieces together.

questions.text: Do you call APIs in your work?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் வேலையில் APIs-ஐ call செய்கிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I call APIs to get data.

reactions.say: APIs are a big part of modern software.
That is fine. Many projects do not need them.

questions.text: Which tool do you use to test an API?
questions.tamil: API-ஐ test செய்ய எந்த tool பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்கள்?
questions.example: I use Postman to test APIs.

reactions.say: Postman is a very popular tool.
Curl is quick and powerful in the terminal.
Those are handy tools too.

questions.text: What is a REST API, and what do GET and POST requests do?
questions.tamil: REST API என்றால் என்ன? GET மற்றும் POST requests என்ன செய்கின்றன?
questions.example: A REST API uses web URLs for actions. GET reads data from the server, and POST sends new data to it.

reactions.say: REST is the most common style on the web.
Those two methods cover most daily work.
Those methods update and remove data.
Each endpoint is a door to a resource.

questions.text: What does JSON look like, and why do APIs use it so often?
questions.tamil: JSON எப்படி இருக்கும்? APIs ஏன் அதை அடிக்கடி பயன்படுத்துகின்றன?
questions.example: JSON stores data as names and values inside curly brackets. It is light, easy to read and works in many languages.

reactions.say: JSON is the common language of APIs.
Key and value pairs are the whole idea.
XML is older and heavier than JSON.
Simple and readable is why people like it.

questions.text: What do the status codes 200, 404 and 500 mean?
questions.tamil: 200, 404, 500 ஆகிய status codes என்ன அர்த்தம்?
questions.example: 200 means success, 404 means the resource was not found, and 500 means there is an error on the server.

reactions.say: 200 is the happy status!
404 is the most famous error on the web.
500 errors need the backend team to check.
Those two relate to login and permissions.

questions.text: How do you secure an API? Explain a few common methods.
questions.tamil: API-ஐ எப்படி பாதுகாப்பீர்கள்? சில பொதுவான முறைகளை விளக்குங்கள்.
questions.example: I use HTTPS, require a token for authentication, check permissions for every request, and validate all input.

reactions.say: HTTPS is the first basic step.
Tokens are the standard way to prove identity.
Authentication and authorization are different things.
Validating input stops many attacks.

questions.text: How do you design API versioning so that old clients do not break when you change something?
questions.tamil: பழைய clients உடையாமல் இருக்க, மாற்றம் செய்யும்போது API versioning-ஐ எப்படி வடிவமைப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: I add a version number in the URL, keep old versions running for some time, and tell clients early before I remove anything.

reactions.say: Versioning protects existing users.
Backward compatibility is very important.
Giving early notice is a respectful habit.
Clients depend on stable APIs.

questions.text: What are the trade-offs between REST and other styles like GraphQL for a project? Which would you choose and why?
questions.tamil: ஒரு ப்ராஜெக்டுக்கு REST மற்றும் GraphQL போன்ற பிற முறைகளுக்கு இடையே உள்ள நன்மை தீமைகள் என்ன? எதை தேர்ந்தெடுப்பீர்கள், ஏன்?
questions.example: REST is simple and well known, but may return too much data. GraphQL lets clients ask for exactly what they need, but it adds complexity.

reactions.say: REST is simple and widely supported.
GraphQL gives clients more control.
Simplicity is often a good deciding factor.
Caching works very naturally with REST.

questions.text: Do you use Git every day?
questions.tamil: நீங்கள் தினமும் Git பயன்படுத்துகிறீர்களா?
questions.example: Yes, I use Git every day.

reactions.say: Git is the daily bread of developers!
It is a good tool to learn well.

questions.text: What is a repository?
questions.tamil: repository என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A repository is a folder that stores our code and its history.

reactions.say: Right, it holds your whole project.
The history is the best part of Git.

questions.text: What does git commit do?
questions.tamil: git commit என்ன செய்கிறது?
questions.example: It saves my changes with a message.

reactions.say: A clear commit message is a gift to your team.
Small commits are easier to review.

questions.text: What is a branch in Git, and why do we create branches?
questions.tamil: Git-இல் branch என்றால் என்ன? நாம் ஏன் branches உருவாக்குகிறோம்?
questions.example: A branch is a separate line of work. We create one for each feature so the main code stays safe.

reactions.say: Branches make teamwork safe.
A branch per feature is a common habit.
Protecting the main branch is wise.

questions.text: How do you create a pull request, and what happens in a code review?
questions.tamil: pull request-ஐ எப்படி உருவாக்குவீர்கள்? code review-இல் என்ன நடக்கும்?
questions.example: I push my branch and open a pull request. Then teammates read my code, comment on it, and approve it.

reactions.say: Code reviews improve quality for everyone.
Constructive comments help everybody learn.
Approval happens before the merge.
Those platforms have nice review tools.

questions.text: What is the difference between git pull and git fetch?
questions.tamil: git pull மற்றும் git fetch இடையே என்ன வேறுபாடு?
questions.example: Fetch only downloads the new changes, but pull downloads them and also merges them into my branch.

reactions.say: Fetch is the safer way to look first.
Pull is quick, but it changes your branch.
Pull does a fetch and a merge.

questions.text: What is a merge conflict, and how do you resolve one calmly?
questions.tamil: merge conflict என்றால் என்ன? அதை அமைதியாக எப்படி தீர்ப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: A conflict happens when two people change the same lines. I open the file, compare both versions, keep the right code and commit.

reactions.say: Conflicts are normal in team projects.
Good communication reduces conflicts.
Editors show conflicts clearly.
Run the tests after resolving, to be safe.

questions.text: Explain the difference between merge and rebase. Which one do you prefer and why?
questions.tamil: merge மற்றும் rebase இடையே உள்ள வேறுபாட்டை விளக்குங்கள். எதை விரும்புவீர்கள், ஏன்?
questions.example: Merge keeps the full history with a merge commit, while rebase moves my commits on top of the latest code for a cleaner line. I avoid rebasing shared branches.

reactions.say: Merge keeps history exactly as it happened.
Rebase makes history linear, but needs care.
A clean history is easier to read.
Never rewrite history that others already use.

questions.text: What branching strategy would you suggest for a team of ten developers, and why?
questions.tamil: பத்து developers கொண்ட குழுவுக்கு எந்த branching strategy-யை பரிந்துரைப்பீர்கள், ஏன்?
questions.example: I would use a main branch with short-lived feature branches and pull requests, because it is simple and keeps integration frequent.

Reviews keep the quality high.

questions.text: What project are you working on now?

questions.example: I am working on a hospital management system.

reactions.say: That sounds like a useful project!

questions.text: How big is your project team?

questions.example: There are eight people in my team.

reactions.say: A team of that size can work closely together.
A large team needs good communication.

questions.text: What is your role in the project?

questions.example: I am a backend developer.

reactions.say: Every role is important for the product.
Testers protect product quality.
Leading a team is a big responsibility.

questions.text: What is the biggest challenge in your current project, and how is the team handling it?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் தற்போதைய ப்ராஜெக்டில் மிகப்பெரிய சவால் என்ன, குழு அதை எப்படி கையாளுகிறது?

reactions.say: Time pressure is a challenge in many projects.
Changing requirements are very common.
Technical issues need patient work.
Communication with clients needs care.

questions.text: How does your team plan its work, for example using sprints or weekly goals?
questions.tamil: உங்கள் குழு வேலையை எப்படி திட்டமிடுகிறது, உதாரணமாக sprints அல்லது வாராந்திர இலக்குகள்?
questions.example: We work in two-week sprints. We plan tasks at the start and review the results at the end.

reactions.say: Sprints give the team a steady rhythm.
Agile methods are common in IT companies.
Regular planning keeps everyone aligned.
Boards make progress visible.

questions.text: Which tools does your team use to communicate and track tasks?
questions.tamil: தகவல் தொடர்புக்கும் வேலைகளை கண்காணிக்கவும் உங்கள் குழு எந்த tools பயன்படுத்துகிறது?
questions.example: We use Teams for chat and meetings, and Jira to track tasks.

reactions.say: Chat tools keep teams connected.

Email is still useful for formal updates.

questions.text: If the client changes the requirements late in the project, how should the team respond?
questions.tamil: ப்ராஜெக்டின் பிற்பகுதியில் வாடிக்கையாளர் தேவைகளை மாற்றினால், குழு எப்படி பதிலளிக்க வேண்டும்?
questions.example: We should understand the reason, estimate the impact on time and cost, and then agree on the priorities with the client.

reactions.say: Showing the impact helps the client decide.
Managing scope is a vital skill.
Clear communication with the client is key.
A formal change request keeps things fair.

questions.text: How do you decide on the technical design of a new feature when team members have different opinions?
questions.tamil: குழு உறுப்பினர்களுக்கு வெவ்வேறு கருத்துகள் இருக்கும்போது ஒரு புதிய feature-இன் தொழில்நுட்ப வடிவமைப்பை எப்படி தீர்மானிப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: We list the options with pros and cons, check them against our requirements, and make a decision together, noting the reasons.

reactions.say: Comparing options keeps debates fair.
A small prototype can settle many arguments.
Writing the decision helps in the future.
Someone must make the final call.

questions.text: What lessons have you learned from a project that did not go as planned?
questions.tamil: திட்டமிட்டபடி நடக்காத ஒரு ப்ராஜெக்டிலிருந்து நீங்கள் என்ன பாடங்களை கற்றுக்கொண்டீர்கள்?
questions.example: I learned to clarify requirements early, share risks quickly, and test sooner so that problems do not pile up at the end.

reactions.say: Clear requirements save so much trouble.

Communication is the lesson in many stories.

questions.text: What is the cloud, in simple words?

questions.example: The cloud means using computers on the internet instead of our own computers.

reactions.say: A simple and clear idea!

questions.text: What is a server?
questions.tamil: server என்றால் என்ன?
questions.example: A server is a computer that gives data to other computers.

reactions.say: Yes, a server is a special computer.

questions.text: What is a website?

questions.example: A website is a group of web pages on the internet.

reactions.say: Simple and right.

questions.text: How would you explain what a database does to a person from a non-technical background?
questions.tamil: தொழில்நுட்ப பின்னணி இல்லாத ஒருவருக்கு database என்ன செய்கிறது என்பதை எப்படி விளக்குவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would say a database is like a big, well-organised notebook where the software stores and finds information quickly.

reactions.say: Good comparison. Easy to picture.
Storing and finding are its two big jobs.
Everything is organised in tables.

questions.text: How do you explain the difference between the front end and the back end of an application?
questions.tamil: ஒரு பயன்பாட்டின் front end மற்றும் back end இடையே உள்ள வேறுபாட்டை எப்படி விளக்குவீர்கள்?
questions.example: The front end is what users see and click. The back end is the hidden part that handles data and the business rules.

reactions.say: Frontend is the face of the product.

The restaurant example is a great way to explain it!

questions.text: How would you explain to a client why a software project takes several months?
questions.tamil: ஒரு மென்பொருள் ப்ராஜெக்ட் ஏன் பல மாதங்கள் எடுக்கும் என்பதை வாடிக்கையாளருக்கு எப்படி விளக்குவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would explain that we plan, build, test and fix in stages, just like constructing a building, so each part must be done carefully.

reactions.say: Building examples are easy for clients to understand.
Showing the stages makes the work visible.
Quality needs time, and clients usually appreciate that.

questions.text: Explain the difference between a monolith and microservices. When would you choose each?
questions.tamil: monolith மற்றும் microservices இடையே உள்ள வேறுபாட்டை விளக்குங்கள். எப்போது எதை தேர்ந்தெடுப்பீர்கள்?
questions.example: A monolith is one big application, simple to start. Microservices split it into small services, which scale well but add complexity. I start with a monolith for small teams.

reactions.say: Monoliths are simpler to build and deploy.

Scaling is the main reason people move to microservices.
More services mean more operational work.

questions.text: How would you explain cloud computing benefits and risks to a business owner who is considering moving to the cloud?
questions.tamil: cloud-க்கு மாற நினைக்கும் ஒரு வணிக உரிமையாளருக்கு cloud computing-இன் நன்மைகளையும் அபாயங்களையும் எப்படி விளக்குவீர்கள்?
questions.example: I would say the cloud saves hardware cost and scales easily, but costs can grow and security still needs attention, so we need a clear plan.

reactions.say: Cost control is a top question for owners.
Flexibility is a major benefit.
Security is a shared responsibility in the cloud.

Closing open tasks shows professionalism.

questions.text: What would make you decide to join us instead of staying where you are?

questions.text: Why do you want to work in our company?

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in five years?

reactions.say: Time with family is important for energy.

Good planning really makes the difference.

questions.text: What kind of work environment helps you perform at your best?
